body:

title: POST PREP — final copy below, post at 9:30
body:
TITLE:
Nobody in home improvement gets paid to say "you don't need that." So I built a free thing that does.

BODY:
Every place you go for home advice makes money when you spend more. Stores sell product. The "free advice" sites sell your info to contractors. Nothing out there is set up to tell you a repair can wait, or that the cheap version is fine.

So I built the opposite. Take a photo of any part of your house and it tells you what's worth doing, what to skip, and what can wait — based on what's actually visible in the photo.

Every result includes at least one thing NOT to buy. That's a rule, not a maybe.

Free, no account. It strips the location data off your photos automatically.

alderprojects.com/check

It's brand new and barely used, so it'll get things wrong. If you try it, tell me what it got wrong about your house — that's the most useful thing anyone can do right now.

Also genuinely curious, unrelated to the tool: what's the worst "the whole thing needs replacing" quote you've ever been given?

MECHANICS: plain URL, no shortener. Flair: Show & Tell (or closest).
IMAGE: only attach a result card from an ORDINARY room you shot for this — not the bathroom/attic test sessions.
DO NOT add a tracking parameter: the site does not read one yet, so it would capture nothing.

title: POST NOW — then live in comments until 11:30
body:
Submit the post from the 8:45 reminder, verbatim. Then stay in the thread until 11:30 and reply to EVERY comment.

The comments are the actual product here — there are ZERO feedback rows in the database, so a stranger telling you what the read got wrong is the most valuable data the business can get today.

As you go, keep a running note of: (1) anything someone says it got wrong, (2) any fix they expected it to catch and it didn't, (3) the exact words they use for the problem. You'll log these tonight.

title: Thread check-in #1
body: Reply to new comments. Upvote good feedback. Anyone who ran a check: ask what the read got wrong — reactions are the training signal.

title: Thread check-in #2
body: Same drill. If the thread died, that's data too — note upvote count + comment count for Friday's review.

title: Harvest the thread — this is the part that isn't a traffic play
body:
Before the thread goes cold, write down three things:

1. UPVOTES + COMMENT COUNT. Two numbers, that's it. Without them you can't compare this post to the next one.

2. EVERY criticism of the read, verbatim. Not paraphrased — their words. These become QA flags and, eventually, curation rules.

3. What people ASSUMED it did that it doesn't. Wrong expectations are a product spec you get for free.

Anyone who actually ran a Check: ask what it got wrong and whether they'd have spent the money. That single question is worth more than the traffic.
